C. arguing that since two things happened at the same time one must have caused the other (This relates to correlation vs. causation, but not specifically *post hoc*).

I. arguing that since two events are unrelated, one cannot have caused the other (This is sound reasoning).

Option A is the most precise definition of the *post hoc ergo propter hoc* fallacy.
